Microsoft attributed the lower Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage to scaling its AI infrastructure, partly offset by efficiency gains in Azure. The filing passages give the 69% level but not the prior-year Microsoft Cloud margin, so I could not quantify the cloud-specific decline. Company-wide revenue grew 14.9% in FY2025. Company-wide gross margin slipped from 69.76% to 68.82%, a fall of about 0.94 percentage points. Company-wide operating margin rose from 44.64% to 45.62%, so the premise of shrinking margins holds only for gross margin, not for operating margin. Capital expenditure rose 45.1% to $64.55 billion.
Microsoft stated that the Microsoft Cloud gross margin percentage decreased to 69%, driven by the impact of scaling its AI infrastructure, offset in part by efficiency gains in Azure. Cost of revenue rose $13.7 billion, or 19%, driven by growth in Microsoft Cloud.
In the Intelligent Cloud segment, Microsoft reported that cost of revenue increased $10.6 billion, or 36%, driven by growth in Azure. Gross margin percentage decreased because of the impact of scaling its AI infrastructure, offset in part by efficiency gains in Azure.
Microsoft said its investments in cloud and AI infrastructure and devices will continue to increase operating costs and may decrease operating margins. It is expanding datacenter locations and server capacity, particularly given the growing demand for AI services.
Company-wide revenue grew about 14.9% in FY2025, from $245.12 billion to $281.72 billion.
Company-wide gross margin was about 69.76% in FY2024.
Company-wide gross margin was about 68.82% in FY2025.
Company-wide gross margin fell by about 0.94 percentage points. This is a proxy for cloud, not a cloud-specific figure.
Company-wide operating margin was about 44.64% in FY2024.
Company-wide operating margin was about 45.62% in FY2025.
Company-wide operating margin rose by about 0.98 percentage points, so the evidence does not show an operating-margin decline at the company level.
Capital expenditure (payments for property, plant and equipment) rose about 45.1% in FY2025, from $44.48 billion to $64.55 billion. This is consistent with the AI and cloud infrastructure build-out, but the filing passages do not link it directly to the margin change.
